sections.heading: What Are Commercial Glass Wall Systems?
sections.body: Commercial glass wall systems are engineered glazing assemblies that replace traditional drywall or opaque partitions with framed or frameless glass panels. These systems can span entire floor plates, divide open-plan offices into focused work zones, or create light-filled lobbies that make a powerful first impression. Common configurations include full-height framed systems with aluminum or steel profiles, frameless all-glass partitions secured with structural silicone or patch fittings, sliding glass wall panels for flexible space division, and storefront-style curtain wall assemblies for exterior-facing applications. In dense commercial corridors like those surrounding the Rosslyn-Ballston corridor, glass wall systems help tenants maximize perceived square footage while maintaining visual connectivity between spaces. Our team assesses your building's structural requirements, layout goals, and aesthetic preferences before recommending the right system configuration for your specific project.

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Glass Type for Your Wall System
sections.body: The glass specified for a wall system significantly affects its performance, appearance, and long-term maintenance requirements. Tempered glass is a common choice for its safety characteristics — when broken, it fractures into small, relatively harmless granules rather than dangerous shards. Laminated glass adds an interlayer that holds the assembly together if the glass is compromised, which is often preferred in high-traffic commercial settings. Insulated glass units, which incorporate two or more panes separated by a sealed air or gas space, are typically used in exterior-facing assemblies where thermal performance matters. Decorative options such as frosted, sandblasted, or ceramic-fritted glass allow for privacy or branding elements within a transparent partition system. Our team discusses the trade-offs of each glass type with clients and provides recommendations based on the specific application, traffic levels, acoustic goals, and design intent of the project — without oversimplifying what is often a nuanced material selection process.

faq.q: How long does it take to install a glass wall system in a commercial space?
faq.a: Installation timelines vary based on the size and complexity of the system. A single-room glass partition can often be completed in one to two days, while a multi-room or full-floor system may require a week or more. We provide a detailed schedule estimate during the quoting process so you can plan around the work.

faq.q: Can glass wall systems be installed in occupied office buildings?
faq.a: Yes. We regularly work in occupied commercial buildings throughout Arlington and structure our installation schedule to minimize disruption. Depending on the scope, work may be phased or scheduled during off-hours to keep your operations running smoothly.

faq.q: What maintenance do glass wall systems require?
faq.a: Glass wall systems are generally low-maintenance. Regular cleaning with appropriate glass cleaners keeps panels looking their best. Hardware components such as hinges, pivots, and track systems may benefit from periodic inspection and lubrication. We can advise on a simple maintenance routine suited to your specific system.

faq.q: Do you handle both frameless and framed glass wall systems?
faq.a: Yes. We install both frameless all-glass systems and framed systems using aluminum or steel profiles. Each approach has its own aesthetic and structural characteristics, and we help clients choose the right configuration based on their design goals, budget, and building conditions.
